subject: keen-code
title: Compact trigger measures the actual serialized outbound request before EVERY tool turn - but tokens stay a len/3 heuristic and provider usage never feeds back
one_why: A mid-ladder rung between history-shape triggers (crush-6) and pi's exact projected context: estimateAnthropicInput JSON-marshals the exact messages about to ship (so pending tool results count immediately), threshold = window - max(4096,w/20) - further 10%, and the boundary is property-tested to the token (85500 fires, 85499 does not) - but usage events incl. cached_tokens (anthropic.go:711-720) are display-only, so unlike cline's token-estimator-feedback the estimator can never self-correct; 5 provider paths re-implement the same trigger inline.

subject: keen-code
title: Dual message cache breakpoints (stable turn-start boundary + last message) cleared/reapplied per turn, with stale-marker stripping asserted at the wire
one_why: Every turn starts from a marker-free clone (clearAnthropicCacheControl), then places system/tools/turn-start/last ephemeral markers; post-compaction the stable boundary resets so breakpoints follow the new prefix; tests capture the actual request params and assert EXACT marker counts (3 normal, 2 one-shot) and that stale pending-state markers are stripped - the test idiom is the portable part, joining the jazz/g3 breakpoint cluster; missing vs 8.5+ rungs: no warming/keepalive and no realized-cache-hit validation.

subject: keen-code
title: Anti-scope-amnesia: session allow-grants are toolName-keyed but structurally never honored for elevated risk, and danger is computed independent of the model's own flag
one_why: Direct counterexample to neovate's approval-scope amnesia (same category-level cache key, wrong handling): `if !isDangerous && sessionAllowedTools[toolName]` means an allow-session for bash NEVER covers a dangerous command - the cache cannot ride a risk-class elevation - and bash.go gates on `isDangerous || IsDangerousCommand(command)` so model under-reporting cannot disarm the prompt (bash_test.go:477 proves the classifier binds with no LLM flag; classifier suite covers compound, subshell, redirection, env-secret forms); hotdog rule: caches may key coarse IF the key's scope cannot widen into a higher risk class without re-prompt.

subject: keen-code
title: Subagent registries ship a hard-wired unconditional AutoApprover - delegated bash/write/edit/MCP never surface a user prompt
one_why: Negative pole of the opencode non-escalation precedent: child registries are constructed with approver=always-true, so containment is only filesystem.Guard + profile tool-list - a dangerous command inside a subagent classifies, requests, and self-approves silently, splitting the user's threat model between parent and child surfaces; bounded (guard, timeouts) so no score dock at the 6-rung, but delegation must inherit the parent's LIVE requester or narrow, never widen.

subject: keen-code
title: Token-map bash classifier with recursive subshell expansion sits between regex deny-lists and grammar parsing - interpreter payloads remain unreachable
one_why: Splits command segments, recurses into subshells, maps base commands + dangerous subcommands + conditional flags + an env-secret regex - meaningfully stronger than substring/regex deny-lists (zot) but, like all corpus deny-lists, `python -c 'shutil.rmtree(...)'` executes unflagged; corpus strictness order: token-map-with-recursion (keen) > regex-denylist > substring; grammar-parsed (maki/codex) still the ceiling.

subject: keen-code
title: Wire-capture test idiom: mock stream seam captures the full outbound request struct and tests assert on the serialized payload
one_why: streamImpl captures anthropic.MessageNewParams and tests marshal it to assert cache-marker counts, absence of top-level cache control, and stale-marker stripping - correctness is pinned at the wire contract rather than internal state, which is why this T1 solo project's 35.9k test LOC actually constrain provider-request behavior (all blocking under go test -race, go.yml:29-30); the cheapest verification-shape upgrade path for subjects stuck at existence tests.
